OpenAI plans to launch its first product this year and release it for sale in 2027, despite facing a second lawsuit over the theft of trade secrets related to its hardware business in just over a year, according to Bloomberg. Here are the details.

First Product Launch Still Planned for 2026

Last Friday, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the company and several former Apple employees of stealing confidential hardware information to advance OpenAI's consumer device business.

The lawsuit details what it calls a "pattern of former Apple employees at OpenAI stealing Apple's trade secrets" and notes that "such misconduct has been normalized and led by example from leadership."

The lawsuit adds to OpenAI's legal troubles in hardware, following another lawsuit previously filed by startup iyO. That case initially involved only trademark matters but was later amended to include allegations of trade secret theft.

Despite the lawsuit news on Friday, OpenAI appears to still be sticking to its hardware development timeline. As Bloomberg notes:

There has been much speculation about OpenAI's specific plans since it announced it would partner with Jony Ive's io Products to create an "AI-first" device.

After the partnership was announced in May 2025, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said OpenAI's first device would be a small, screenless wearable that could be worn around the neck, equipped with cameras and microphones to capture the user's surroundings, with a smartphone handling computing and display functions.

OpenAI has hinted that it plans to launch multiple devices rather than a single product, and stated in court filings in the iyO lawsuit that the first product is not the in-ear or wearable device that was speculated when the partnership was announced.
